nodes.label: Every motor-vehicle driver must comply with the applicable speed limits.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: This general compliance requirement has no accepted competing permission to ignore an applicable speed limit.

nodes.label: The speed at which a vehicle travels affects the driver’s control of it.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: This general speed-and-control statement is not contrasted by a competing control claim in the accepted facts.

nodes.label: The handbook lists fifteen miles per hour as the maximum in a school zone with a posted speed limit.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: The posted school-zone maximum and business/residential default concern different locations. Preserve the school posting condition and the different-sign qualification.

nodes.label: For a business or residential area, the handbook gives a thirty-mile-per-hour maximum unless a sign sets a different limit.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: The posted school-zone maximum and business/residential default concern different locations. Preserve the school posting condition and the different-sign qualification.
Business/residential and public-highway defaults apply in different settings; both retain their stated posted-limit qualifications.

nodes.label: For public highways, the handbook gives a fifty-five-mile-per-hour maximum unless another limit is posted.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: Business/residential and public-highway defaults apply in different settings; both retain their stated posted-limit qualifications.

nodes.label: For rural interstate highways, the handbook gives a seventy-five-mile-per-hour maximum unless signs state otherwise.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Do not drive below a posted minimum speed.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: When no minimum speed is posted, choose a speed that does not obstruct normal traffic flow.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Adjust speed for adverse conditions, the type of vehicle and the need to prevent a crash.

nodes.label: The driver is responsible for ensuring a parked vehicle creates no hazard.

nodes.label: Choose a parking position far enough from moving lanes to avoid interfering with traffic.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: A parked vehicle should be visible to drivers approaching from either direction.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Use a designated parking area whenever possible.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Apply the parking brake whenever you park.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Leave a parked manual-transmission vehicle in gear.

nodes.label: Check nearby traffic before opening a vehicle door.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: If possible, get out of a parked vehicle on the curb side.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: When you must exit on the street side, check traffic before getting out.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: Do not leave ignition keys inside a parked vehicle.

nodes.label: If parking on a roadway is necessary, position the vehicle as far from moving traffic as possible.

nodes.label: If you must park on a roadway with a curb, position the vehicle as near to the curb as possible.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

nodes.label: The staged handbook directs a driver parking on a hill to turn the wheels sharply toward the road edge or curb.

nodes.label: Parking inside an intersection is prohibited.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: Parking inside an intersection and parking near its crosswalk are distinct prohibited locations. Do not replace the inside prohibition with the distance rule.

nodes.label: Parking on a crosswalk or on a sidewalk is prohibited.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: Parking on a crosswalk or sidewalk differs from the stated clearance around an intersection crosswalk. Keep on-location and nearby-distance rules separate.

nodes.label: Do not park in a construction zone when the vehicle would block traffic.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: The construction-zone prohibition specifies blocking traffic; the posted no-parking rule is separate. Preserve the condition without inventing general parking permission when it is absent.

nodes.label: The handbook prohibits parking within thirty feet of a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: Traffic-control devices and intersection crosswalks have different stated parking clearances. Keep each distance with its object.

nodes.label: The handbook prohibits parking within twenty-five feet of an intersection crosswalk.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: One equal authored emphasis unit per retained stable accepted fact; this is teaching policy, not an official exam weight.

confusable_with.why: Parking inside an intersection and parking near its crosswalk are distinct prohibited locations. Do not replace the inside prohibition with the distance rule.
Parking on a crosswalk or sidewalk differs from the stated clearance around an intersection crosswalk. Keep on-location and nearby-distance rules separate.
Traffic-control devices and intersection crosswalks have different stated parking clearances. Keep each distance with its object.

nodes.label: Keep parked vehicles at least fifteen feet from a fire hydrant.

nodes.label: The handbook prohibits parking within fifty feet of a railroad crossing.
